quote_text:
Yeah, such a great performance. Obviously, St  Johnstone made it really difficult for us in  
that first period. And it is, when you're  playing against that sort of man-to-man,  
you have to work so hard to rotate and be  flexible in your movement to create the  
space. But once we then did that for the  first goal, and we got the runner off the  
marker and Callum finishes, then from that  we really set the tempo of the game. And so  
it was very impressive and a big applause to the  players because they were so good in the game.
That's something we put emphasis on this  season—even if the breakthrough takes a while,  
that once you get it, the foot goes to the floor  again. The game can almost be won within the next  
10 minutes or so. Yeah, I spoke before to the  players about... my thoughts going into this game  
was this was about having the humility to get the  work in. Because once you're a team that’s won it,  
then it becomes even harder because you have to  work even harder, because teams are trying to  
stop you, and they have that fight and  they put that extra percent in to stop you.  
So it’s having that humility to run,  to work. And then after you do that,  
it’s then about the ambition in the  game. And that’s what we showed today.
Even in the first half, the second half we come  out and our messaging was to make sure we retain  
the tempo, keep the speed in the game, keep the  pace in the game, attack the game, press the game,  
and hopefully more chances will come. And they  did come but we didn’t quite finish them. But  
that’s a huge testament to the players because, as  I said, we needed to respond from the St Johnstone  
game which, two weeks ago, wasn’t acceptable for  our club. But the response of the players—now  
they’ve had two games done by half-time—but  still showed the ambition to keep going.
How important has your captain been this season  
arriving in big goalscoring moments  as well as his general performance?
Yeah, he's just such a special player. I've  had him in two spells now and managed him  
for so many games. He's a real tactical  decision-maker in the game. He sets the  
tempo for the team. He's a coach on the pitch  for me. He knows the patterns that we want and  
he identifies the moments when to step in.  Because you're playing against man-to-man,  
there’s little patterns that free you up to  be going forward. And he's done it so many  
times for me, and especially here at Hampden,  where he gets such important goals. First one,  
creates. The second one, just a brilliant captain  of this club. And yeah, he was so good today.
Potentially two games now,  
Brendan—from six in eight years—which is  quite remarkable. Your team look on it now?
Yeah, I think it’s been such a long season  and with so many games. And I think we've  
had one or two performances within that,  which is natural, that maybe weren't quite  
at our best. But what I've had with nearly  two years of this team is just making sure  
that mentality—you’ve got to keep pushing.  You know, it's the time of the season where  
the trophies are there. The supporters  want it, we want it, but then it's about,  
you've got to perform. So yeah, so we're into  another final. That was the big ambition from  
today. And it gives us that opportunity  against Aberdeen in a month or so’s time.
But now we go into a little sort of  mini league where we want to be the  
best in that little league. And that  next game is Dundee United and get  
the result to draw a line under the league.  So yeah, really exciting end to the season.
Was that motivating yesterday—clearly?
Yeah. Do I say 3.1 will be as well?
Yeah, listen, of course it’s nice when it comes to  as an individual. But for me, it’s what’s best for  
Celtic and us winning and winning the trophies.  Because it’s not so much the trophies for me on a  
personal level—it’s the hard work that goes into  it, the values that are there, and the idea of  
how we work and how we play and how we coach the  players every day. So that’s what’s more important  
to me. But of course, for the club and the history  and the supporters, getting the trophy is key.  
So for us, we’ve got two more to win, and we’ll  recover and get ready to finish off the league.
For Adam?
Yeah, had a couple of the moments where he  could have been in there. But it was—yeah—it’s  
where he has to be. It’s where our  strikers—they get so many cross balls,  
low crosses into the box—and that’s where he  needs to be in that moment. So great move,  
great run, cross, and he was there to finish.
Yeah, I think when you're playing against  that system, it's so important that your  
two centre-halves are able to step in and  distribute the ball with that quality. And  
Liam did that. He's a fantastic player. Liam  makes a great ball, but it only goes in there  
because of the run. Riel's run was there,  and he squares it, and it’s a good finish.
That’s 21 times you’ve been here and  you’ve won. It’s incredible for anyone.
Yeah, I think I’ve always tried to approach these  like it’s my very first time. I never get tired of  
it. I never expect it. The preparation and the  mentality—because I know each game is harder,  
because the teams are really motivated to  win. But there’ll be nobody more motivated  
to win than me to keep the club succeeding,  demanding more from the players and our staff.  
And that’s why we have the success. Nobody  goes through the motions here at Celtic.  
We never get too carried away when we win. You  know, we have to keep with humility because we  
know we have to work even harder. But our ambition  is there to win—and win for this great club.
title: Brendan Rodgers Post Match Press Conference | St Johnstone 0-5 Celtic.
